Class ScreenFrames

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ScreenFrames
public final class ScreenFrames extends Object
A vanilla container screen made taller or shorter at a seam (7.4.0): its frame gains (or loses) by rows at row seam of its own layout, so screens of nearly one size can be made exactly one, and a tab row standing on their frames doesn't move as one opens in place of another. 
// A mod's screen, 170 tall, made 166 like vanilla's: four rows out of the gap above its inventory.
ScreenFrames.stretch(MyBoxScreen.class, 76, -4);

Vanilla's screens are one size already

MenuKit makes every vanilla container screen whose frame is nearly 166 tall exactly 166, the size of nearly all of them (the inventory, the crafting table, the furnaces, the dispenser, the enchanting table, the anvil and the rest), with no declaration:
  • The shulker box, 167 tall with an image of 166, loses the blank row under its image.
  • The 3-row chest (chests, barrels, the ender chest), 168 tall with an image of 167, loses that blank row and one row of the gap under its slots, so its inventory slots and label sit where the shulker box's do, its inventory where every 166 screen's is.
  • Every other chest size (the double chest's 222) loses only its blank row.
So a vanilla screen's frame is exactly what it draws, and the moving frame of a screen opened in place of another lands on the art. A mod's own seam is added to MenuKit's.
  • The screen's size is vanilla's plus by, centered by vanilla as any screen of that size is, so it sits exactly where a vanilla screen of that size does: the inventory and a shulker box share one frame on every window.
  • Above the seam everything keeps its place in the frame: slots, labels, the player model, the recipe book button. From the seam down everything is by lower in the frame: slots (another mod's added to the menu included) and the "Inventory" label.
  • The screen's own image draws in parts with the seam row repeated by times between them, or with -by rows from the seam left out. OptiGUI's swap and a resource pack's texture apply to each part as to the whole.
  • Exactly the class given; a subclass keeps its own size. While the container region takes the screen's image, its panels draw in place of the image; the region lays out from the stretched size, slots and label.
  • Another mod reading the screen's bounds (topPos, imageHeight) reads the stretched frame; one placing something by vanilla's fixed offsets from the top, below the seam, is by off.

A grid that scrolls when the frame doesn't fit (7.4.0)

scrollsWhenShort(ModeScope, ScreenMatcher) turns it on for the screens a mod chooses; MenuKit never does on its own. On such a screen, while its frame wouldn't fit the window, its own container grid scrolls inside the frame and the frame is as much shorter, so the whole screen fits: 
// A large chest on a short window: its six rows scroll, the inventory stays put.
ScreenFrames.scrollsWhenShort(ModeScope.BOTH, ScreenMatcher.only(ContainerScreen.class));
  • When. The frame (its seams included) and the tab rows on its top and bottom edges are taller than the window less the 4 px margins the container region keeps, the same block the shared centering rule centers. Read every frame; a resize lays it out again. On a window it fits, the screen is vanilla's, pixel for pixel, and nothing on it is moved.
  • What scrolls. The grid's rows, by pixels, inside the frame, as few given back as make the screen fit, never under three; the title, the player's inventory, the hotbar and the rest of the frame stay put. The scrollbar's lane is beside the grid, the frame that much wider. A window too short even for three rows scrolls the column as the container region does.
  • How. It is the container region, fitted, with the screen's own grid as its first section, a SlotScroll: a row cut at the edge shows, hovers and takes clicks only where it shows, a row out of view is inert, the wheel scrolls it, a shift-click into a hidden row scrolls there, and the screen's bounds are the frame's.
  • Its slots are vanilla's. Each one shown sits where it is drawn, so a recipe viewer or a mod reading slot.x/y finds it there; one scrolled out of view is parked off the screen; all of them go back to vanilla's places once the frame fits again or the screen closes.
  • Which screens. Any container screen whose own container is a full grid of 18 px slots under its title at the frame's content edge, as a chest's, a barrel's, a shulker box's or a mod's chest's are (slot x 8, y 18). A screen without one is left as it is, and so are the player's own inventory screens. While another mod's section shows on the screen too, the grid's section is first.

Declare from your client initializer: frames freeze with every other declaration.
